Carlos: Quick follow-up from the streaming/iteration workshop earlier today. Wanted to capture the decision sketch while it's fresh.
Anya: good idea. we still need a single conceptual model for clients across languages.
Pri: Recap: we defined three resumability levels: NONE (no resume), PAGE (opaque page tokens), ITEM (per-item sequencing + acks).
Taylor: Language ergonomics summary: python -> sync/async pairs, ts -> async-iterable oriented, go -> channels + context cancellation.
Carlos: My leaning: default to PAGE for simplicity/compat. ITEM as opt-in when the workload needs exactly-once-ish semantics.
Olga: Right. ITEM forces decisions about dedupe and lease semantics. We should avoid making ITEM the default.
devops-bot: upload: streaming-proto-v2.pb completed
Anya: Transport mapping thoughts:
- HTTP paged GETs -> PAGE only. cheap, caches, works everywhere.
- gRPC bidi streaming -> supports ITEM (ack path) + lower latency.
- WebSocket -> browser-friendly ITEM-like behavior, but operationally closer to grpc.
Pri: SDK surface proposal (two-level):
1) High-level listing APIs: listPages()/list() that yield pages with page_token.
2) Streaming low-level: stream() that yields items plus an ack callback for ITEM semantics.
Taylor: TS example pattern to avoid mutation:
for await (const { item, ack } of client.stream('list')) {
  handle(item);
  if (shouldAck) await ack();
}
Carlos: Python sketch (both sync & async):
```py
for itm in client.stream('list', page_size=200):
    process(itm)
    if error_after_processing:
        itm.ack()  # opt-in
```
Taylor: For Go: channel of struct { Item T; Ack func() error } and callers range over the chan. Provide helper wrappers for common patterns.
Anya: Retry semantics: PAGE calls are idempotent (retry safe). ITEM streaming retries need to exchange last-acked token on reconnect so we don't re-deliver ACKed items.
Pri: Lightweight approach: SDK persists last-acked monotonic token locally (file/sqlite). On reconnect we send that token and server resumes after it. Keeps server state tiny.
Olga: Document warning: if client crashes before persisting token, clients may see duplicates. Recommend durable ack persistence for strong guarantees.
Carlos: Operational knobs: server must keep page tokens stable for a configurable window (default 24h). Also expose a capability flag in /models or /meta so SDKs can discover supported resumability and transports.
Anya: Security/permissions: ack endpoints must validate auth (obviously) and rate-limit ack traffic to avoid abuse.
Pri: Edge cases:
- When page token expires mid-retry, return explicit error code for client to restart from beginning.
- ITEM-level reorder: servers should include per-item seq ids; clients must not assume strict ordering over retries unless documented.
Taylor: Action items:
- Anya -> draft RFC doc: enumerated resumability levels, transport mapping, SDK shapes + examples (due Thu)
- Taylor -> prototype TS `stream()` wrapper that yields {item, ack} and exercises reconnect logic (PoC in repo)
- Carlos -> sync with runtime team to add stable page token support for 24h and capability flags
- Pri -> draft SDK recommendation for local ack persistence patterns (fs/sqlite)
devops-bot: scheduled maintenance 2026-03-25 01:30 UTC
Olga: I'm fine with the plan. small note: make sure we include metrics (re-deliveries, ack-latency) in console.
Carlos: Agreed. I'll add a telemetry section to the RFC. Thanks everyone.
Anya: No objections here :+1:
Pri: Starting the RFC now, will ping when ready for review.
Taylor: I'll drop the TS sketch into the hack folder and link it in the RFC.
Carlos: Closing thread for now. We'll use the RFC as the single source of truth.
